title: Insider PowerToys version tricks the Microsoft store into thinking that PowerToys is not installed
next_action: Approve the package-identity investigation and request stable/Insider identity evidence.

judgment.rationale: The report identifies a stable-to-Insider Microsoft Store transition followed by loss of installed-state recognition. Package identity, sparse registration, or intentional channel separation must be distinguished before changing packaging.
evidence: Affected build is 0.101.2432 Insider from Microsoft Store.
The Store no longer recognizes PowerToys as installed after the update.
No comments, diagnostics, assignee, linked fix, or duplicate are present.
Installer code contains explicit sparse Package Identity MSIX registration and removal paths.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve controlled package-identity investigation and request before/after Store identity data.

fix_assessment.rationale: No public open or merged fix covers this Store stable-to-Insider recognition issue.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Store-recognizable package identity across supported channel upgrades
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the Insider package identity or sparse registration is incompatible with the stable Store product, or the transition leaves registration incomplete. It may instead be intentional channel separation.
plan: Record Package Full Name, Family Name, publisher, version, registration, and Store state before and after stable-to-Insider installation.
Compare stable/Insider manifests and installer identity inputs.
If identities should be shared, preserve compatible identity and register correctly during upgrade.
If channels are intentionally separate, document the expected Store behavior instead of changing identity.
verification: Install Store stable, record identity, install Insider, restart Store, and verify recognition.
Verify rollback or upgrade back to stable.
Confirm package scope and uninstall behavior remain correct.

confidence.rationale: Package identity is the likely boundary, but the report has only a screenshot and no before/after identity metadata.

issue_context.summary: After updating to Insider, Microsoft Store presents PowerToys as not installed.
known_information: Affected build is 0.101.2432 Insider from Microsoft Store.
The symptom follows an Insider update.
No discussion, diagnostic, assignee, or linked remediation exists.
Installer code has sparse Package Identity MSIX install/uninstall paths.
inferences: Package family, publisher, identity, version, or registration may not match the Store's expected upgrade relationship.
The behavior may be intentional if Insider is a separate Store product.
issue_context.analysis: A controlled package comparison can distinguish a fixable registration regression from expected channel behavior without risking installed-package identity changes prematurely.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body, labels, timeline, and absence of discussion.
Focused installer areas are CustomAction.cpp and Product.wxs package-identity registration.
No public fix attempt or duplicate was found.

information_gaps.information: Stable and Insider Package Full Name, Family Name, publisher, version, and registration state.
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines identity mismatch versus incomplete registration.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Record `Get-AppxPackage` output and Store state before and after the transition.

information_gaps.information: Whether stable and Insider are intended to share Store ownership.
information_gaps.why_needed: Prevents changing identity when channel separation is intentional.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the supported channel-transition behavior from current packaging/release guidance.

design.root_cause: Unconfirmed Store package identity or sparse-registration mismatch during stable-to-Insider transition.
evidence: Store recognition is lost after Insider update.
Installer includes explicit sparse package identity registration.

affected_files.purpose: Installs and removes sparse Package Identity MSIX registration.
Schedules package identity installation/removal during MSI upgrade.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The installer registers and removes sparse package identity during install/upgrade, but channel compatibility is unverified.
implementation_steps.change: Compare identities first; if sharing is intended, preserve compatible identity and ensure registration runs on upgrade without crossing user or channel scope.
implementation_steps.code_block: before = identity + registration + StoreState; install Insider; after = identity + registration + StoreState; if shared: preserve identity and register on upgrade
edge_cases: Stable and Insider may intentionally use different identities.
Per-user and machine registration must remain isolated.
Uninstall must not remove another channel's package.

verify: Capture identity and Store state before and after the transition.
Run the existing installer/package validation workflow.
Verify Store recognition or document intentional channel separation.
risks: Changing package identity can strand installed packages or break Store updates.
alternatives: Require uninstall/reinstall; rejected because it does not resolve a compatible identity regression.
Force Store cache refresh; rejected because package identity or registration may be the cause.

comment.body:
Thanks for the report. To resolve the recorded uncertainty, please provide:

1. Stable and Insider Package Full Name, Family Name, publisher, version, and registration state. Collection: Record `Get-AppxPackage` output and Store state before and after the transition.
2. Whether stable and Insider are intended to share Store ownership. Collection: Confirm the supported channel-transition behavior from current packaging/release guidance.

reproduce.version_requirement: Current Store stable followed by current Insider build
prerequisites: Windows test environment with Microsoft Store access.
steps: Record package identity and Store recognition.
Install the current Insider build over stable.
Restart Microsoft Store and open the PowerToys page.
Record package identity, registration, and installed-state recognition.
If supported, upgrade back to stable and repeat.
reproduce.expected_result: Store recognition remains consistent if both channels share product identity; otherwise the supported channel limitation is confirmed.
